title: Zanzibar: Love Letters from the Spice Island
author: Kivara Concierge
excerpt: Beyond the beaches lies an island woven with history, spice, and romance. Our guide to the most enchanting experiences in Zanzibar for couples who seek the extraordinary.
content:
Zanzibar has a way of slowing time. The island operates on what locals call "Zanzibar time" — a gentle rhythm that resists hurry. Within days of arriving, you will find yourself calibrated to its pace: breakfasts that stretch into mid-morning, afternoons lost to books and hammocks, dinners that begin at sunset and end when the last candle flickers out.

This is the Spice Island, where the air is perfumed with cloves, nutmeg, cinnamon, and vanilla. Where turquoise waters lap against powder-white sand beaches shaded by coconut palms. Where Swahili, Arab, Indian, and European influences have woven a culture as rich and layered as the spice trade that built it.

For couples, Zanzibar offers something rare: a destination that combines beachfront indulgence with cultural depth, luxury with authenticity, adventure with utter relaxation. Here is our guide to experiencing the island at its most romantic.

Stone Town: The Soul of the Island

Before you lose yourself to beach life, spend at least one night in Stone Town. This UNESCO World Heritage site is a labyrinth of narrow alleys, carved wooden doors, and bustling markets. The history here is layered — Arab, Persian, Indian, African, European — woven into the architecture, the food, the very air.

Wander through the winding streets hand in hand, discovering hidden courtyards, spice shops piled high with colourful powders, and galleries showcasing contemporary Zanzibari art. Visit the Old Fort, the House of Wonders, and the Anglican Cathedral built on the site of the old slave market — a poignant reminder of the island's complex history.

As evening falls, head to the rooftop of Emerson on Hurumzi for sundowners overlooking the rooftops of the old city, the call to prayer echoing across the stone buildings as the sun sinks into the Indian Ocean. Dinner at the Zanzibar Serena Inn's terrace restaurant, with the sea breeze and the sound of waves, is the perfect end to a Stone Town day.

The Beach Life

Zanzibar's beaches are legendary for good reason. Each coast offers a different character, and choosing the right stretch of sand for your romance is essential.

Bwejuu — The Palms Zanzibar

Bwejuu Beach on the southeast coast is recognised by Condé Nast Traveller as one of the top 30 beaches in the world. Here, The Palms Zanzibar offers the island's most exclusive beachfront experience — just seven villas, each with a private plunge pool, personal butler, and a thatched beach banda on the sand. This is adults-only, ultra-luxury, with gourmet dining and premium beverages included. With a maximum of 14 guests at any time, The Palms offers a level of privacy unmatched on the island. Explore The Palms →

Kendwa — Kilindi Zanzibar

On the north-west coast, Kilindi Zanzibar's fifteen white-domed Pavilion villas are set within 50 acres of tropical garden. Each villa has its own private plunge pool and a separate rainfall shower room with spectacular ocean views. Originally designed for ABBA's Benny Andersson, the property achieves the perfect marriage between Scandinavian minimalism and Middle Eastern architectural drama. A dedicated butler is assigned to every villa. Explore Kilindi →

Michamvi — Xanadu Luxury Villas

Nine uncompromising villas on Michamvi's pristine white sand beach, each with a Swahili name — Umande (dew), Alfajiri (dawn), Mawingu (clouds), Kimwondo (stars). Each villa has its own plunge pool, personal butler, and all-inclusive cuisine prepared by an international chef. A member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World. Explore Xanadu →

Bwejuu — Baraza Resort & Spa

Baraza is Zanzibar's most architecturally dramatic resort — inspired by Arabian palaces with Swahili influences, its 30 villas cluster around courtyards with fountains and tropical gardens. The resort sits on the same stretch of award-winning Bwejuu Beach as The Palms, with access to shared facilities including a PADI dive centre, gym, and tennis court. Explore Baraza →

Kizimkazi — The Residence Zanzibar

On Zanzibar's tranquil southern coast, The Residence offers sixty-six sprawling villas set within 32 hectares of tropical gardens. Each villa has its own private pool, outdoor shower, and a terrace that opens onto pristine beach. The overwater spa crowns the experience — treatment rooms suspended above the Indian Ocean where the rhythm of the waves becomes part of your restoration. Explore The Residence →

Beyond the Beach

A spice tour is essential — Zanzibar is the Spice Island, after all, and the scent of cloves, nutmeg, and cinnamon hangs in the air. Visit a working spice farm, taste fresh vanilla pods straight from the vine, and learn how the spice trade shaped the island's history and culture. Many tours include a traditional Swahili lunch cooked with the spices you have just harvested.

The Jozani Forest, home to the endemic red colobus monkey, offers a completely different side of Zanzibar. Boardwalks wind through a groundwater forest where ancient trees are draped with ferns and monkeys leap between branches overhead. It is a serene, mystical experience that contrasts beautifully with the coastal life.

For the ultimate romantic experience, book a private sunset dhow cruise along the coast. These traditional wooden vessels have sailed the Indian Ocean for centuries, and there is something timeless about watching the sun sink into the sea from the deck of a dhow, champagne in hand, your partner beside you, the only sound the creak of the mast and the lapping of water against the hull.

Zanzibar's Culinary Scene

Zanzibari cuisine is a reflection of its history — a fusion of African, Arab, Indian, and Portuguese influences, united by the island's extraordinary spices. The street food scene in Stone Town's Forodhani Gardens is not to be missed: grilled seafood skewers (mishkaki), Zanzibari pizza (a thin crepe stuffed with spiced meat and vegetables), and fresh sugarcane juice.

For fine dining, the island's luxury hotels offer world-class cuisine. The Palms' gourmet dining is included and changes daily. Kilindi's all-inclusive package covers three meals daily plus drinks and sundowners. At Baraza, the Stone & Spice Cafe serves Swahili fusion in a garden setting.

When to Go

Zanzibar is lovely year-round, but the sweet spot is June to October and December to February, when the weather is dry and the seas are calm. The long rains (March to May) bring lush vegetation and lower rates, while the short rains (November) are typically brief and refreshing. For the best of both worlds — excellent weather and fewer crowds — consider June or September.
